html:
The Saffarids were a Persian dynasty from Sistan, in what is now eastern Iran and southwestern Afghanistan, that ruled much of Iran from 861 and held Sistan until 1002. They are shown here in 900.

The founder, Yaqub ibn al-Layth, was a coppersmith, saffar in Arabic, who rose by leading local fighters against bandits and Kharijite rebels. With his army he conquered Sistan, Kabul, Kerman and Fars, and in 873 ended the rule of the Tahirids in Khorasan. In 876 he marched on Baghdad itself but was beaten not far from the city by the Abbasid army.

His brother Amr ruled next, until the Samanids defeated and captured him in 900. After that the Saffarids held only Sistan, until Mahmud of Ghazni took it in 1002. They were among the first native Iranian dynasties after the Arab conquest, in the period called the Iranian Intermezzo, and Yaqub's court was among the first to favour poetry in Persian rather than Arabic.
